key_insight: Delafossite and ordered rock-salt ABO2 oxides can be nearly as stable as infinite-layer oxides, with nickelates showing especially strong competition and a distinct dz2-dominated electronic structure.
engineering_relevance: This narrows the synthesis design space for layered oxide devices by identifying which cation/anion combinations are most likely to stabilize or destabilize infinite-layer phases relevant to superconducting thin films.
method: High-throughput first-principles simulations across ABO2 oxides
Thermodynamic phase stability comparison for four layered oxide motifs
Electronic-structure analysis of the competing phases
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a compiled stability phase diagram and electronic-structure comparisons across the periodic table, highlighting La-Ni as the thermodynamic optimum for the infinite-layer motif and stronger delafossite competition in Ni, Pd, and Pt systems.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on computational thermodynamics and electronic structure, so experimental thin-film growth, substrate effects, and kinetic barriers may still shift the realized phase stability.
paper_title: Delafossites as an unexpected competing phase to infinite-layer oxides
